title: Circuit-depth optimization of quantum partial-search algorithms
authors: Yan-Bo Jiang, Xiao-Hui Wang, Kun Zhang, Vladimir Korepin
abstract: Grover's algorithm is optimal in terms of oracle queries. We can trade accuracy for speed, which gives rise to the quantum partial-search algorithm. The partial-search algorithm is implemented using two kinds of Grover operators, global and local, where the former is the standard Grover operator for full search and the latter has a diffusion operator acting on the search subspace. The global-local-global sequence, also known as the Grover-Radhakrishnan-Korepin (GRK) algorithm, has been proved optimal in the oracle-query metric. In this work, we show that the alternating sequence of global and local Grover operators, formed by repeatedly applying a fixed product of global and local Grover operators, can achieve a lower expected circuit depth than the GRK algorithm. Through systematic analysis, we obtain its exact success probability, expected depth, and asymptotically optimal parameters. We derive the boundary, characterized by the ratio between the depths of the oracle and the global diffusion operator, separating the depth-optimal and oracle-optimal partial-search algorithms. When the depths of the oracle and the global diffusion operator are comparable, our proposed alternating partial-search sequence can reduce the minimum expected circuit depth by more than 20\% compared with the GRK algorithm.
summary: This paper optimizes the circuit depth for quantum partial-search algorithms by proposing an alternating sequence of global and local Grover operators. By analyzing the expected circuit depth, the authors demonstrate that this new sequence can significantly outperform the established GRK algorithm in depth-constrained scenarios. This advances the practical implementation of quantum search algorithms by providing a depth-optimal alternative.
main_problem: The paper aims to optimize the circuit depth of quantum partial-search algorithms, moving beyond the established optimality criteria based solely on the number of oracle queries.
main_result: An alternating sequence of global and local Grover operators can achieve a significantly lower expected circuit depth (over 20% reduction) compared to the standard Grover-Radhakrishnan-Korepin (GRK) sequence when the oracle and diffusion operator depths are comparable.
method: The authors systematically analyze the expected circuit depth, $E_\ell(S)$, for various sequence structures, comparing the depth-optimal alternating sequence ($S_A$) against the query-optimal GRK sequence ($S_G$).
model_or_system: The model is a quantum partial-search algorithm applied to a database of size $N=2^n$, utilizing global ($G_n$) and local ($G_m$) Grover operators. The analysis compares depth-based optimization against query-count optimization.
key_observables: Expected circuit depth ($E_\ell(S)$), success probability ($	ext{Pr}(S)$), and the ratio of operator depths ($\alpha$).
important_parameters: The ratio $\alpha$ between the oracle and global diffusion operator depths, and the block size $b$ relative to the total size $N$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on asymptotic approximations for large $N$ and $K$, and the comparison is made between depth-optimal and query-optimal regimes.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the geometric paths of the GRK sequence versus the depth-efficient alternating sequence in the invariant subspace. Figure 3 presents a phase diagram mapping the optimal sequence choice across different depth ratios ($\alpha$).
paper_structure: The paper reviews the GRK algorithm's query optimality, proposes the depth-efficient alternating sequence ($S_A$), and then systematically analyzes $S_A$ to derive its exact success probability and expected depth, establishing the boundary separating depth-optimal and oracle-optimal regimes.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses resource optimization in quantum computation, providing concrete, improved circuit implementations for search problems that are crucial for quantum algorithm development.
